Scope and field of application

3

Definitions

This international Standard specifies a format and recording standard for g-track, 12,7 mm (0.5 in) magnetic tape to be used for data interchange between information processing systems, communication systems, and associated equipment utilizing the 7-bit `coded character set (see IS0 646). its extension in IS0 2022 where required, and the &bit coded character set (see IS0 4873). Magnetic labelling for use on magnetic tape is the subject of IS0 1001. The magnetic tape and reel to be used shall conform to IS0 1854.
NOTE - Numeric values in the St and/or Imperial measurement system in this International Standard may have been rounded and therefore are consistent with, but not exactly equal to, each other. Either system may be used, but the two should be neither intermixed nor reconverted. The original design was made using the Imperial measurement system.

For the purpose of this International Standard, the followin! definitions apply.

5.3

Average

flux transition

spacings

The following measurements shall be made after interchange using a tape recorded at a density of 178 ftpmm (4 521 ftpi). Thl
nominal flux transition spacing at this density shall be 5,618 pm (221.2 pin) subject to the following variations. 5.3.1 The long term average (static) flux transition spacing shall be within f 4 % of the nominal spacing. This average shall b# measured over a minimum of 5 x 106 successive flux transitions. ".3.2 The short term average (dynamic) flux transition spacing, when referred to a particular flux transition spacing, is the average a that flux transition spacing and the preceding flux transition spacing. The short term average flux transition spacing shall be within the limits of f 6 % of the long term average flux transition spacing , / In addition, the rateof change of the short term average flux transition spacing shall not exceed 0,2 % per flux transition spacing

5.4

Instantaneous

flux transition

spacings

The instantaneous spacing between flux transitions may be influenced by the reading and writing processes, the pattern recordec (pulse crowding effects) and other factors. Instantaneous spacings between flux transitions shall meet the following conditions, when tested on the reference read chain (sea annex B). 5.4.1 At the nominal maximum density of 356 ftpmm (9 042 ftpi) the spacing dt between successive flux transitions shall be bs tween 48 % and 52 % of the corresponding short term average flux transition spacing determined at 178 ftpmm (4 521 ftpi).

Minimum

signal amplitude

A tape to be interchanged shall contain no flux transition in more than one track since the last MARK 1 control sub-group, the base-to-peak amplitude of which is less than 15 % of half the standard reference amplitude.

ECC character

The ECC character shall be calculated separately for each group (data group, residual group and CRC group). In each case, 7 polynomials D, to D7 shall be formed, the coefficients pf which shall be the 8 bits of each byte in positions I to 7. The coefficients of polynomial D1 shall be the bits in position 1, those of polynomial D2 shall be the bits in position 2, etc. The parity bit in track 4 shall not be part of the ECC character generation. These bits shall be allocated to the polynomials as follows :

Residual character

Polynomials Mj shall be formed, the coefficients of which are the bits in each byte. The coefficients of polynomial MI shall be the bits of the byte in position 1 of the first data group, those of polynomial M2 shall be the bits of the byte in position 2, etc., up to M,, for the n characters to be considered. 10.3 Synchronization sub-group (SYNCI
A SYNC shall be a (llllll

10

Control

sub-groups

10.4

MARK

1 control rub-group

A control sub-group shall comprise five consecutive storage rows having, with the exception of TERM 2, the same bit pattern in each track.

A MARK 1 shall be a (00111) control sub-group.

10.5 10.1 Terminator control sub-groups (TERM)

MARK

2 control

sub-group

A MARK 2 shall be a (11100) control sub-oroup.

A TERM 1 shall be a (10101) control sub-group. It shall be placed at the BOT end of each storage block Isee 11.2.1). A TERM 2 shall be a (1010X) control sub-group, where X represents a bit which restores for each track the magnetic remanence to the erase state (see 5.7). It shall be placed at the EOT end of each storage block (see 11.2.7).

10.6

END MARK

sub-group

An END MARK shall be a (11111 I control sub-group. It has the same pattern as a SYNC sub-group, but not the sama function.

11 10.2 Second control sub-groups (SEC) 11.1
A SEC 1 shall be a (01111) control sub-group. It shall follow TERM 1 (see 11.2.1) at the BOT end of each block. A SEC 2 shall be a (11110) control sub-group. It shall precede TERM 2 (see 11.2.7) at the EOT end of each block.

Storage

block

Data portion

The data portion of a storage block shall accommodete, in group-coded form, 8 minimum of 18 data bytes and a maximum of 8 19 data bytes. However, larger blocks may be usad by agreement between the interchanging parties.

11.2.4

Number N 158

of data storage groupr

N<

In this case, the last data storage group shall be followed by an END MARK control sub-group preceding the residual group and there shall be no RESYNC burst.

Due to the insertion of an ECC character after each seventh data byte, to the 4-bit to 5-bit conversion and to the RESYNC burst after each 158th data storage group, the maximum density of recorded data is less than the maximum physical recording density of 356 ftpmm (9 042 ftpi) by a factor of 7 4 -xXx 8 158 160 giving 246 data bytes per millimetre (6 250 bytes per inch).

N>

158

In this case, a RESYNC burst shall be inserted after every 158 data storage groups and an END MARK control sub-group shall be inserted after the last data storage group. However, if N is a multiple of 158, there shall be no RESYNC burst after the last data storage group but only an END MARK control sub-group. NOTE - When a RESYNC burstis present,a MARK 1 and a M'ARK2 controlsub-groupbracket all sequencesof 156 data storagegroups. 11.2.5 Residual storage group and CRC storage group

Tape

format

The beginning of the tape before the first preamble shall present typical areas defined in 12.1 to 12.5 inclusive. 12.1 Density identification area (ID burst)

The residual storage group and the CRC storage group shall follow the END MARK inserted after the last data storage group. 11.2.6 MARK 2

The ID burst shall be an area characterized by bit pattern ~100100100...~ in track 6, i.e. by a density of 119 + 12 ftpmm (3 014 f 300 ftpi) and by erasure in all other tracks. It shall begin at least 43 mm (1.7 in) before the trailing edge of the BOT marker and continue past this edge.

12.2

Gap Gl

A MARK 2 control sub-group shall follow the CRC storage group and precede the postamble.

The ID burst shall be followed by a gap Gl of at most 8636 mm (3.4 in).

12.3 Automatic Read Amplification (ARA) Area
The ARA Area shall comprise an ARA level burst followed by an ARA identification burst. 12.3.1 ARA level burst

-

recording of bit pattern (1111.. .I in all other tracks.

A length of at least 635 mm (0.250 in) shall ba arror-fraa in dl tracks. (See 13.2.)

12.4 Gap 62
Between the end of the ARA ID burst and the firat atoraga block there shall be a gap 62 of the sama length as an interblock gap.

The ARA level burst, which follows gap Gl shall be characterized by bit pattern (1111.. .I recorded in all tracks, i.e. by a density of 356 ftpmm (9 042 ftpi). It shall begin at least 36 mm (1.5 in) and at most 109 mm (4.3 in) after the leading edge of the BOT marker. It shall end at least 241 mm (9.5 in) and at most 292 mm (11.5 in) after this edge. Accordingly its minimum length is 132 mm (5.20 in) and its maximum length is 254 mm (10 in).

Annex A Transportation
(This annex does not form part of the standard.1

A.1

Environment :

It is recommended that during transportation the tapes are kept within the following condiis
temperature : 4 to 32 "C MO to 90 OF) relative humidity: 20 to 50 %

A.2

Hazards

Transportation of data-bearing magnetic tape involves three basic potential hazards :

A.2.1

Impact

loads and vibrations

Those forces which could cause damage to the reel, or movement within the tape pack, with consequential loss of wlnd tension. Recommendations a) b) c) The free end of the tape should be secured to prevent any tendency to unwind. A rigid plastic container free from dust or other extraneous matter should be used. The plastic container(s) should be fitted into a rigid box containing adequate shock absorbent material.

d) The final box should have a clean interior and a lid construction that provides sufficient sealing to prevent the ingress of dirt and water. e) f) The orientation of the reels within the final box should be such that their axes are horizontal. The final box should be clearly marked to indicate its correct orientation.

A.2.2

Extremes

of temperature

and humidity

Those extremes which could set up stresses within the body of the tape. Recommendations a) Extreme changes in temperature and humidity should be avoided wherever possible.

b) Whenever a tape is received, it should be conditioned in the operating environment (see 4.1) for a period of 2 to 12 h, depending upon the type of transportation used and the likely extent of exposure to conditions out&e the operating environment. A.2.3

Effects of stray magnetic

fields

Those effects which would possibly cause corruption of data. Recommendation A nominal spacing of not less than 80 mm (3.15 in) should exist between the magnetic tape reel end the outer surfaceof the final container in which case it is considered that the risk of corruption will be neglllible.

Annex 6 Procedure and equipment for measuring flux transition spacing

(This annex forms part of the standard.)

B.l

General

8.2.2

Head

The equipment normally used for recording interchange tapes (tape transport) at 246 cpmm (6 250 cpi) shall be used for recording the tape under test. The tape shall be written in any start-stop mode of operation compatible with system operation. The full length of tape of 732 m (2 400 rt) shall be recorded with the following test patterns.

There are no absolute output voltage requirements. However, the output voltage shall be sufficient to avoid problems due to a ' low signal-to-noise ratio. The gap shall be less than 1,143 urn. The transfer function of the head shall be such that :

In the frequency range of 27 to 540 kHz, the magnitude characteristic shall be within 1 dB from a + 6 dB/octave line. Sinewave
